readings.verb: copy pattern to opposite edge and bridge
readings.reading: A small multi-colour pattern sits at the left edge. It is copied to the right edge, and the gap between the two copies is filled in each row with that row's first (and last) pattern colour.
readings.why: output = left pattern + per-row fill + same pattern at right edge; pattern's first and last columns are equal

readings.verb: copy pattern to opposite edge and bridge
readings.reading: A small multi-colour pattern sits at the left edge. A copy of it is placed flush with the right edge, and the gap between the two copies is filled, row by row, with that row's first-column colour.
readings.why: on every row, output = pattern + (row's first colour repeated) + pattern, total width unchanged

readings.reading: The coloured block at the left edge is copied flush to the right edge, and the gap between the two copies is filled, row by row, with that row's first-cell colour.
readings.why: output row = block + row[0] repeated + block, on every pair

readings.verb: copy to far edge and bridge
readings.reading: The multi-coloured pattern at the left edge is copied flush to the right edge, and each row's gap between the two copies is filled with that row's first-column colour.
readings.why: output = input pattern at left + same pattern at right, every background cell between them in a row takes the row's edge colour

readings.verb: copy to far edge and bridge
readings.reading: The multi-coloured block at the left edge is copied flush against the right edge, and each row's gap between the two copies is filled with that row's edge colour (the block's first and last columns share a colour).
readings.why: output = block at left, block at right edge, and every row's middle cells equal the colour of the block cells bounding them

readings.reading: Each solid 8 rectangle is repainted: its four half-by-half quadrants become 6 (top-left), 1 (top-right), 2 (bottom-left), 3 (bottom-right), and the interior inset 2 cells from every edge becomes 4.
readings.why: every rectangle cell is recoloured by its position inside its own rectangle; background unchanged

readings.reading: Each solid colour-8 rectangle is recoloured by position: its four quadrants become 6 (top-left), 1 (top-right), 2 (bottom-left), 3 (bottom-right), and the inner rectangle inset by 2 cells on every side becomes 4.
readings.why: every rectangle cell's new colour depends only on its position inside its own rectangle; background unchanged

readings.reading: Each solid 8 rectangle is recoloured by position: an inner core inset by 2 cells becomes 4, and the remaining 2-wide rim is split into quadrants: top-left 6, top-right 1, bottom-left 2, bottom-right 3.
readings.why: every 8 cell is recoloured by its position in its rectangle; background unchanged

readings.reading: Every solid 8-rectangle is repainted: a 2-cell-wide outer band split into quadrants coloured 6 (top-left), 1 (top-right), 2 (bottom-left), 3 (bottom-right), and the inner area coloured 4.
readings.why: each rectangle keeps its footprint; colour depends only on cell position within its rectangle

readings.reading: Each solid 8 rectangle is recoloured by quadrant: top-left 6, top-right 1, bottom-left 2, bottom-right 3, and its core (cells at least 2 in from the rectangle's edge) becomes 4.
readings.why: every 8 cell is recoloured by its quadrant or core position; background unchanged

readings.verb: mark side toward nearest border line
readings.reading: Two opposite border lines of different colours bound the grid. Every 1 cell gets one neighbour cell (on the side facing the nearer border line) painted with that line's colour.
readings.why: each 1 cell gains exactly one adjacent cell coloured like the closer border line, on the side facing it

readings.reading: Two opposite borders are full lines of two colours. Next to every isolated 1-cell, on the side facing the nearer of the two border lines, a cell of that border's colour is added.
readings.why: each marker gains exactly one neighbour, coloured as and placed toward the closer border line; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Two opposite border lines have different colours; each 1 cell gets one new cell next to it, on the side towards the nearer border line, in that border's colour.
readings.why: every 1 cell gains exactly one neighbour coloured like its nearer border

readings.reading: Two opposite border lines have different colours; each isolated 1-cell gets one neighbouring cell, on the side facing the nearer border line, painted that line's colour.
readings.why: every marker gains exactly one adjacent cell coloured as the closer border line, on the side toward it

readings.reading: Two opposite grid edges are full lines of different colours; next to every colour-1 cell one cell is painted on the side facing the nearer edge line, in that line's colour.
readings.why: each 1 cell gets exactly one new neighbour, toward the closer coloured edge, with that edge's colour

readings.reading: Every object moves right by a distance equal to its own bounding-box width, keeping its shape.
readings.why: each object reappears unchanged, displaced right by its width

readings.verb: shift each object right by its width
readings.reading: Every object is shifted to the right by a distance equal to its own bounding-box width.
readings.why: each object keeps its shape and rows; its column offset increases by its width

readings.reading: Each object moves right by a distance equal to its own width.
readings.why: each object keeps its shape and rows; its column offset equals its width

readings.reading: Each 8-object is shifted right by a distance equal to its own bounding-box width.
readings.why: every object keeps its shape and row; its new left column = old left column + width

readings.reading: Every object slides right by exactly its own width (bounding-box width).
readings.why: each object keeps its shape and its new left edge is at old left + width (it lands just right of where it was)

readings.reading: Several overlapping, partly hidden octagon rings of different colours (plus scattered noise cells) lie on a background. Each ring is completed to the same 6x6 octagon outline and the rings are stacked vertically in a 6-wide output.
readings.why: output height = 6 x number of rings; each 6x6 block is the complete ring of one colour on the input background

readings.reading: Several overlapping octagonal rings of different colours (plus scattered noise cells) are drawn on a background. The output stacks one clean 6x6 ring per colour vertically, topmost (least occluded) ring first, on the input's background colour.
readings.why: output is N stacked 6x6 canonical rings, one per ring colour, in occlusion order

readings.verb: list ring colours as clean rings
readings.reading: Several noisy copies of one octagonal ring shape, each in its own colour, overlap in a chain among scattered noise cells; the output stacks a clean 6x6 ring of each ring colour vertically, in chain order.
readings.why: output is a 6-wide column of clean rings, one per ring colour

readings.reading: Several overlapping, partly hidden octagon rings (6x6 outline) of distinct colours sit on a noisy background; each ring is completed and the rings are stacked vertically in a 6-wide output on the background colour, noise dropped.
readings.why: output is k stacked 6x6 tiles, each the canonical octagon in one ring colour on background

readings.reading: The noisy grid hides several partial octagon rings (6x6 ring shape) of distinct colours; the output stacks one clean copy of the ring per colour vertically on the background, ordered by their position in the input.
readings.why: output height = 6 x number of ring colours; each 6x6 block is the ring template in one ring colour

readings.reading: A 2x2 block of four colours in the centre is pushed outward: each cell moves to the grid corner on its own side, and the centre becomes empty.
readings.why: the four colours appear exactly at the four grid corners in the same relative arrangement; all else background

readings.reading: A 2x2 block of four colours sits in the centre of a 4x4 grid. Each of its cells moves out to the grid corner nearest it and the centre is cleared.
readings.why: output corners hold the central block's colours in the same relative arrangement; everything else is background

readings.reading: The 2x2 block of four colours at the centre of a 4x4 grid is pulled apart: each cell moves diagonally out to the grid corner nearest it.
readings.why: the four colours appear only at the four corners, each at its own diagonal corner

readings.reading: The four cells of the central 2x2 block each move diagonally out to the nearest grid corner.
readings.why: each single-cell object keeps its colour and ends at the grid corner nearest to it; the centre is cleared

readings.reading: The 2x2 block in the centre of the 4x4 grid is pushed apart: each of its cells moves to the grid corner on its side.
readings.why: each block cell's colour appears at the corresponding grid corner; all else background

readings.reading: Green (3) cells that touch another 3 cell orthogonally turn 8; lone 3 cells (no orthogonal 3 neighbour) stay 3.
readings.why: every non-zero cell with a same-colour orthogonal neighbour maps 3 -> 8; everything else unchanged (note: 3 is the majority colour in some pairs, so px with C > 0 is used instead of cell)

readings.reading: Colour-3 cells that are 4-connected to at least one other 3 become 8; isolated 3s (no orthogonal 3 neighbour) stay 3.
readings.why: every 3 cell with an orthogonal 3 neighbour becomes 8; nothing else changes (diagonal-only contact does not count)

readings.reading: Every 3 cell that has a 3 as an orthogonal neighbour (i.e. belongs to a 4-connected group of 2 or more) becomes 8; lone 3s stay.
readings.why: key 3->8 on cells with a same-colour 4-neighbour; diagonal-only contact does not count

readings.reading: Every 3-cell that belongs to a 4-connected group of two or more cells turns 8; lone 3-cells stay 3.
readings.why: every fg cell with a same-colour 4-neighbour goes 3 -> 8; nothing else changes (diagonal-only contact does not count)

readings.reading: Colour-3 cells that belong to an orthogonally connected group of 2 or more become 8; lone 3 cells (no orthogonal 3 neighbour) stay 3.
readings.why: every 3 cell with an orthogonal 3 neighbour becomes 8 (key 3->8); nothing else changes

readings.reading: A horizontal and a vertical line cross. A 3x3 square ring of 4 is drawn around the crossing cell, overwriting the line cells there; the crossing cell itself keeps its colour.
readings.why: the unit is a 3x3 ring of 4 with a transparent centre, centred on the one cell whose four orthogonal neighbours are all non-background

readings.reading: A vertical and a horizontal line cross. The eight cells around the crossing become 4, leaving the crossing cell itself unchanged.
readings.why: the 8 neighbours of the line crossing are colour 4; every other cell is unchanged

readings.reading: A vertical and a horizontal line cross; a 3x3 square ring of 4 is drawn around the crossing cell, whose own colour is kept.
readings.why: the 8 cells around the crossing become 4; the crossing cell and all other cells are unchanged

readings.reading: A vertical and a horizontal line cross; the 8 cells around the crossing become 4, forming a 3x3 ring, while the crossing cell keeps its colour.
readings.why: one 3x3 ring of 4 (centre transparent) centred on the line intersection; all other cells unchanged

readings.reading: A full vertical line crosses a full horizontal line; the 8 cells around the crossing are painted 4, the crossing cell keeps its colour.
readings.why: the 8 neighbours of the full-row/full-column intersection are colour 4; nothing else changes

readings.verb: join box openings with a band
readings.reading: Two 3x3 boxes of 2 with a 5 centre each have one gap in their wall. The gaps are filled with 4 and a thick 4-coloured band is drawn joining the two gaps, running through the background between the boxes (bounded by the box strips on the non-gap sides).
readings.why: only background cells (and the two gap cells) change, all to 4, forming one connected region touching both gaps

readings.reading: Two 3x3 colour-2 frames with a 5 centre each have one gap in their outline. A 4-coloured corridor is drawn from each gap outward and the two corridors are joined by a filled 4 rectangle spanning the space between the frames; frame cells are not overwritten.
readings.why: 4 cells form one connected filled region touching both gaps; frames and background elsewhere unchanged

readings.reading: Two 3x3 boxes of 2 with a 5 centre each have one open side; the openings are filled with 4 and joined by a solid 4 rectangle spanning from just outside one opening to just outside the other, except cells lying behind either box.
readings.why: only background cells inside the bridge become 4; the boxes are unchanged

readings.reading: Two 3x3 2-frames with a 5 centre each have one gap; a band of 4 is filled from each gap out and across the space between the two frames, joining them, without overwriting the frames.
readings.why: only background cells (and the gap cells) become 4; the 4 region is connected and touches both openings

readings.reading: Two 3x3 colour-2 boxes with a 5 centre each have one missing edge cell (a door); the door cells and a rectangular corridor of 4 joining the two doors' outsides are filled, leaving the area behind each box (the side opposite its door) empty.
readings.why: all filled cells are 4, lie in that corridor, and the boxes are untouched

readings.reading: From the 2 cell on the bottom row a two-cell-wide staircase of 2 climbs diagonally up-right to the top/right border; when a 1 cell blocks the path the staircase steps around it and continues.
readings.why: only background cells change, all to 2, forming a staircase from the 2 to the border that never covers a 1

readings.reading: From the single 2 cell on the bottom row a two-cell-thick diagonal staircase of 2 is drawn up and to the right until the border; where the path would hit a 1 cell it is pushed to go around (beside) the obstacle and continues diagonally.
readings.why: the 2 path is a connected up-right staircase from the source to the border that never covers a 1 cell

readings.verb: draw thick diagonal ray around obstacles
readings.reading: From the single 2 on the bottom row a two-cell-wide diagonal band of 2 runs up and to the right until the border; where a 1 blocks it, the band steps right past the 1 (the row below gains a cell to bridge it) and goes on.
readings.why: the band never overwrites a 1 and reaches the border

readings.reading: From the 2 on the bottom row a 2-coloured staircase (two cells per row) climbs up-right to the top/right edge, sidestepping around any 1 cells it meets.
readings.why: every row above the source holds the staircase cells in colour 2; 1 cells stay unchanged

readings.reading: From the 2 cell on the bottom row a two-cell-thick staircase of 2s climbs up-right to the top/right edge; when its next cell is a 1, the staircase shifts right past the 1s (widening the row below) and continues.
readings.why: every row above the source holds a contiguous run of 2s continuing the diagonal, never overwriting 1s
